title: Study on the Directivity and Signal Processing of Hybrid Acoustic Vector Sensor Array

title: Insight Into Split Beam Cross-Correlator Detector With the Prewhitening Technique
authors: Tianyu Chen; Yanqun Wu; Wen Zhang; Wen Chen; Jun Wang; Zhengliang Hu
description: 分裂波束处理方法已广泛应用于线阵宽带信号的方位估计。它们可以以降低处理增益为代价实现高方位分辨率。分裂波束交叉相关器检测器（SBCD）是其中一种方法，是从两个子阵列的波束对之间冗余的二维互相关中获得互相关序列。 当SBCD与广义互相关（GCC）中的预白化技术相结合时，显示出一些有利于方位估计和检测的独特输出特征，如低输出背景、与功率无关的输出、强调弱目标的能力、抑制强干扰以及抵抗空间光谱中光栅瓣混淆现象。本文旨在通过理论和仿真揭示这些特征及其背后的原因。南海268.75m阵列的实验结果验证了现有理论，并表明预白化技术的SBCD可以提高弱宽带目标的direction-of-arrival（DOA）估计和检测性能。在实时应用的效率和鲁棒性方面，它在实际水下环境中显示出巨大的潜力。

title: 基于小波降噪和Gammatone滤波器的水下目标特征提取与识别
authors: 刘继恒,张文,曾新吾,等

description: 本文提出了一种联合信号处理框架，先通过小波软阈值降噪（使用db8小波基、无偏风险估计阈值）对水下目标信号进行预处理，再使用Gammatone滤波器组（24个子带）进行频域分解，有效提升了在低信噪比环境下的特征提取能力。结果表明，对于相同信噪比的含噪信号，在进行小波降噪后，通过Gammatone滤波器组 处理后的信号的识别率要比未做降噪处理的信号高，同时对于信噪比大于或等于0的含噪信号，本文提出的方法具有较好的噪声鲁棒性，且识别性能良好。

title: Sound source identification in the shallow water using the coherence of the vector field
authors: Yanqun Wu, Wen Zhang, Yu Chen, Wei Qiu, Hao Wu and Zhengliang Hu, "
publication: 引用：Yanqun Wu, Wen Zhang, Yu Chen, Wei Qiu, Hao Wu and Zhengliang Hu, "Sound source identification in the shallow water using the coherence of the vector field," 2018 10th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP), Hangzhou, China, 2018, pp. 1-4, doi: 10.1109/WCSP.2018.8555910
description: 浅水声源识别对后续目标检测和定位算法的性能至关重要。然而，由于水下无源声源往往距离较远，隐藏在嘈杂的环境噪声中，因此很难解决。本文提出了压力与粒子速度不同轴之间的相干性，用于识别三种来源，即近场的头顶噪声、远处的船只噪声和近/远有源。从湖泊试验数据中发现，不同类型的源，压力与粒子速度三个轴之间的相干性不同。此外，矢量传感器的z轴有利于收集从表面传播到底部的开销噪声。声矢量传感器不仅提供声场的方向性，还提供嵌入声场矢量特性的更多独特信息。

title: An Interference Suppression Based Bearing-only Multiple Target Tracking for Passive Sonar

description: 本文提出了一种基于干扰抑制的纯方位多目标跟踪方法（IS-BOT），通过将多目标跟踪问题分解为多个并行的单目标跟踪问题，并引入外部干扰抑制模块，利用特征子空间重构技术消除非目标干扰，从而提升目标方位估计精度。其主要贡献在于构建了闭环反馈结构，实现了干扰抑制模块与跟踪模块之间的实时信息交互，并结合预测功能有效解决了目标航迹交叉问题，海试验证表明该方法能显著平滑航迹、提升跟踪精度。

title: Joint Algorithm Based on Interference Suppression and Kalman Filter for Bearing-Only Weak Target Robust Tracking
authors: Wen Chen; Wen Zhang; Yanqun Wu; Tianyu Chen; Zhengliang Hu
description: 针对水下弱目标存在干扰时的纯方位跟踪（BOT）中跟踪轨迹不连续和目标丢失等问题，提出了一种基于干扰抑制（IS）和卡尔曼滤波（ISKF）的联合算法。在所提出的算法中，为了平滑弱目标的损坏轨迹，提高跟踪精度，建立了连接IS模块和卡尔曼滤波（KF）模块的反馈结构。此外，该反馈结构使轴承轨迹的测量结果在IS模块和KF模块之间实时共享。在ISKF联合算法中，采用IS模块作为预处理模块消除干扰功率，采用KF模块作为跟踪器获得弱目标的方位轨迹。在初始步骤中，使用传统波束形成（CBF）方法估计粗目标方位和干扰方位。在更新步骤中，利用IS和KF联合更新弱目标的精确BOT轨迹。此外，当目标与干扰相交时，借助KF的预测模型，ISKF联合算法仍能有效跟踪弱目标。最后，海试结果表明，该算法比仅KF能够实现更准确、更鲁棒的实时跟踪，这得益于IS模块和KF模块之间的反馈。

description: 本发明涉及一种固定与机动协同的海洋立体同步观测系统以及方法，系统包括包括：固定节点；机动节点；由固定节点和机动节点协同配合来覆盖节点之间的空白区域和观探测盲区；舰载无人机，用于搭载固定节点和机动节点并投放至预设位置；水面舰船，水面舰船被配置为前进时通过携带的声源持续发射水声信号，以及收集固定节点信息和机动节点信息，结合观测任务对机动节点的航行轨迹和固定节点参数进行调控，以时刻维持对目标海洋水体的设定覆盖精度。本发明构建由机动节点和固定节点协同配合的立体同步观测网络，相较于传统的海洋环境调查方法和海洋观测网络更加高效、灵活，能够获取更大范围、分辨率更高和更完备的时空匹配环境数据。

authors: 史剑，张文，王宁，杜辉，余乾坤，郭子龙，朱卓锋，刘永鹏，王玉宏，刘宇昂，王陆昕

title: Performance Analysis and Comparison of Two Deep Learning Methods for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation with Observed Data
authors: Shuo Liu, Wen Zhang *, Junqiang Song, Jian Shi, Hongze Leng and Qiankun Yu
description: The paper systematically compares CNN and LSTM backbones for DOA estimation to clarify architecture-dependent performance and real-data generalization. Models are trained on CSDMs from simulated ULA signals and evaluated across SNR, element spacing, snapshots, array size, and angular resolution. Both exceed 98% accuracy at a 1° interval under baseline conditions; LSTM is more robust below −20 dB SNR, while CNN gives finer angular resolution. Four boundaries are identified: half-wavelength spacing is optimal, −20 dB SNR is a crossover, 32 snapshots marks sufficiency, and 8 elements is a performance turning point. Models trained only on single-target simulations generalize to multi-target SWAP data without domain adaptation.

title: Research on the Response of the Acoustic Structure in the Upper Ocean during Hurricane Transit
authors: Wen Zhang 1,* , Boyuan Duan 1 , Jian Shi 1,** , Peng Jiang 1 , Qiankun Yu 1 , M.V. Subrahmanyam 2,***
description: The study investigates how hurricane transit changes upper-ocean acoustic structure relevant to underwater communication and target detection. Using NOAA hurricane tracks and underwater-glider observations during three consecutive 2017 North Atlantic hurricanes, it determines hurricane–glider distances, derives temperature/salinity-driven sound-speed profiles, and examines acoustic characteristics before, during, and after transit. The acoustic structure begins to change when the hurricane is about 2000 km from the glider, with different responses for left- and right-side approaches. Above and below the main sound channel, profile shapes remain broadly consistent, but acoustic intensity/gradient is stronger for left-side hurricanes and weaker for right-side hurricanes, including an increase in positive gradient intensity on the left from about 0.0228 to 0.092 s⁻¹.

title: In situ RbPbI3 filler for high-performance carbon-based perovskite solar cells
authors: Xuewen Liu a,1 , Sheng Wu a,1 , Yanhui Wang a , Wen Zhang b , Jicai Lang a , Chongyang Xu a,**,  Eun-Cheol Lee c,*
description: The paper reports an in situ RbPbI₃ interfacial filling strategy for high-performance carbon-based perovskite solar cells. Using excess PbI₂ as the lead source, residual PbI₂ is converted into a rubidium-based perovskite phase, reducing its detrimental effects while filling grain boundaries, smoothing the perovskite surface, and improving contact among the triple-cation perovskite, P3HT, and carbon electrode. The optimized CPSCs achieve a champion PCE of 18.81%, much higher than the 14.07% reference devices. Unencapsulated modified devices also show markedly better ambient stability, retaining photovoltaic performance for nearly 300 h at 25 °C and 30–40% relative humidity. The work offers a scalable interfacial-engineering route toward efficient and stable CPSCs.

title: A Trace-Normalized Adaptive Loading Method for Weak Target Direction-of-Arrival Estimation for Underwater Acoustic Arrays
authors: Shuo Liu；Wen Zhang*；Yun Zhao；Zikun Meng；Qiankun Yu；Yan Liu
description: The paper proposes the Trace-Normalized Adaptive Loading method for weak and adjacent underwater acoustic target DOA estimation under low SNR, strong interferers, and limited snapshots. Building on trace-normalized diagonal loading, TNAL is systematically validated on the SWellEx-96 Event S5 dataset with deep and shallow sources towed by a single body. For the North and South horizontal linear arrays, TNAL achieves a 95.80% dual-target resolvable ratio and about 3 dB higher average peak prominence than traditional methods, improving target-separation clarity. The study also reports a previously unobserved bearing deviation between co-towed sources, challenging the assumption of identical bearing trajectories and offering new insight for underwater acoustic data interpretation.

title: Deep Sequence Learning-Based Joint Range and Depth Estimation for Underwater Acoustic Source Localization
authors: Zikun Meng；Wen Zhang*；Jian Shi*；Shuo Liu；Qiankun Yu；Yan Liu
description: The paper proposes a deep sequence-learning framework based on a time-encoded Transformer for joint range–depth estimation of moving underwater acoustic sources in shallow water. Instead of treating snapshots independently, the end-to-end regressor uses self-attention to extract global spatial features and capture continuous source kinematics, reducing sensitivity to environmental mismatch in traditional MFP. A two-stage simulation-to-reality training paradigm is adopted and evaluated on the real-world SACLANT Elba-93 VLA dataset. The model achieves a 2D localization RMSE of 13.17 m at about 7 km range, tracks continuous trajectories reliably, and remains robust under partial sensor dropouts, supporting practical dynamic underwater localization.

title: Research on a small-sized extremely low-Frequency  underwater acoustic source based on the  electromagnetic pulse mechanism
authors: Yun Zhao；Shuo Liu；Jiahao Huang；Wen Zhang
description: The paper proposes a miniaturized extremely low-frequency underwater acoustic source based on the electromagnetic pulse mechanism for unmanned-platform applications. A capacitor discharges through a coil, inducing eddy currents in a nearby metal plate; the electromagnetic force drives plate vibration and radiates pulsed sound, while periodic switching forms an equal-interval pulse train. A circuit–electromagnetic–vibration–acoustic multiphysics model and prototype are developed. Measurements show pulse-train operation generates 10–50 Hz line spectra and harmonics matching the repetition frequency; excessively high repetition weakens enhancement because the capacitor cannot recharge in time. Single-pulse spectra depend on the electromagnetic force spectrum and plate frequency response, while parameter optimization and burst sounding enhance selected low-frequency lines.

title: Analysis of the Adaptability and Application of Matched-Field Processors for Stationary and Maneuvering Targets in Shallow Water
authors: Zikun Meng , Wen Zhang , Jian Shi, Shuo Liu and Qiankun Yu
publication: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
description: Using data from the Elba-93 sea trial, this study compares five matched-field processors. The results show that, for a stationary target under severe environmental mismatch, Bartlett and MVDR are more robust; for a maneuvering target with insufficient snapshots, MUSIC is prone to trajectory jumps, whereas MVDR provides the most stable tracking with the lowest errors, while RCM offers a balance between robustness and computational efficiency.

title: Transformer-based joint two-dimensional range and depth synchronous localization of underwater acoustic target
authors: Zikun Meng, Wen Zhang,Jian Shi, Yan Liu, Shuo Liu, and Qiankun Yu
publication: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 2026, Vol.160: 2480–2494.
description: To address the susceptibility of conventional matched-field localization to environmental mismatch in complex shallow-water environments, a Transformer-based method is proposed for two-dimensional joint range–depth localization of underwater acoustic targets. The model is trained on simulated data generated by the KRAKEN underwater acoustic model and tested on real sea-trial data from Elba-93, with comparisons against Bartlett, MVDR, SA-MVDR, 1D-CNN, and MLP methods. The results show that the proposed model achieves significantly lower errors than conventional matched-field methods and other neural-network baselines under the experimental settings considered in this study. Further single-hydrophone experiments indicate that, after pretraining on full-array simulated data, the model can still maintain low two-dimensional localization errors when tested with only a single hydrophone, providing a new research direction for sparse-array and single-hydrophone underwater acoustic localization.

title: 基于光纤布拉格光栅的压力式海洋波浪高度传感器
authors: 刘兆坤 1 ，杜大伟 1 ，赵强 1，2 ，陈东营 1 ，惠力 1 ，张文 3 ，孙鹏 1，2 ，郭风祥 1
description: 本文提出基于光纤布拉格光栅的压力式海洋波高传感器，用于近岸实时测量；有限元优化膜片与横梁结构，P-FBG测压、T-FBG温补。标定灵敏度−9.486 nm/MPa，量程0~0.3 MPa；提出平滑先验零线法减少零点遗漏。外场结果与SBF3-2浮标趋势一致，相关系数超0.85，具无源、抗电磁干扰、传输快等优点

title: 海洋精细化漂流浮标观测网络实验
authors: 李宾１ 张文１∗ 厉运周２ 赵强２ 徐登科１
description: 设计精细化漂流浮标及组网观测系统，采用分离式抗风浪结构、低功耗组件与LoRa/北斗双天线，经实验与湖试验证温压测量精度、防水和抗风浪性能。基于LoRa动态路由构建4节点10 km网络，丢包率<0.1%、时延<200 ms；FFT显示温度准稳态、压力噪声较高，提出滤波/小波降噪，支撑可扩展立体监测。

title: Bayesian Optimization-Tuned machine learning for underwater acoustic target localization
authors: Yan Liu,1 Wen Zhang,1,a) Jian Shi,1 Peter Gerstoft,2 Haiqiang Niu,3 Qiankun Yu,1 and Zikun Meng1
publication: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
description: The paper proposes a Bayesian-optimization-tuned machine-learning approach for underwater acoustic target localization, addressing MFP’s sensitivity to environmental noise and inefficiency with large-scale data. Using the October 26, 1993 Elba-93 shallow-sea trial environment, KRAKEN generates simulated training data over range–depth grids. MFP is compared with k-nearest neighbor and support vector regression under different hyperparameter-tuning strategies. Machine-learning methods achieve higher localization accuracy than MFP, identifying a target at 5.6 km range with error below 0.1 km and 79 m depth with error below 0.5 m. Bayesian optimization is also more efficient than alternative tuning methods.

title: Design and Testing of Nanovolt-Level Low-Noise Ag-AgCl Electrodes for Expendable Current Profilers
authors: Wen Zhang 1,* , Jian Shi 1 , Xiaoqian Zhu 1 , Zibo Lu 2 , Huanrui Liu 1 and Xinyang Zhu 1
description: The paper designs and tests nanovolt-level low-noise Ag-AgCl electrodes for expendable current profilers, whose performance depends strongly on electrode precision and stability. Four electrode pairs are compared: two custom commercial pairs, one self-developed pair, and one improved self-developed pair. The powder-pressing fabrication process of the self-developed electrode is described. Experiments evaluate self-noise, power spectral density, and frequency response under different conditions. Without an external electric field, Electrodes I–III show 1 Hz PSDs of tens of nV/√Hz, while the improved Electrode IV reaches only a few nV/√Hz and maintains a basically stable response in the XCP-critical 13–18 Hz band, meeting sea-trial requirements.

title: Applications of Harmonic Analysis in the Processing of Marine Environmental Data
authors: Li, Bin (1); Wu, Shenye (1); Zhang, Wen (1); Wu, Sheng (2); Zhao, Qiang (3, 4); Cui, Lin (5); Ling, Chen (1)
description: The paper compares Fourier series analysis and harmonic analysis for extracting periodic components from marine environmental time series. Fourier methods are constrained by harmonic frequencies and therefore fit non-harmonic tidal constituents poorly, whereas harmonic analysis specifies target frequencies and applies least-squares fitting. Its key contribution is a comparative framework that clarifies the theoretical distinction and quantitatively demonstrates harmonic analysis’s advantage using sea surface temperature and sea level data. Results show markedly lower fitting errors for non-harmonic components such as M2 and K1 tides, offering methodological support for refined marine data processing.

title: A review of ocean current measurement technologies
authors: Zhang, Jiawen (1); Cai, Zixuan (1); Xie, Wenbin (1); Zhang, Wen (1); Ling, Chen (1); Liu, Xuanjun (2
description: The review summarizes the principles, technical characteristics, and historical development of mechanical, electromagnetic, acoustic, and optical current meters, comparing their advantages and limitations for marine dynamic-environment observation. It argues that, despite progress, China still faces gaps in development and industrialization: mechanical and electromagnetic instruments trail high-end international products in accuracy, weak-signal processing, and sensor integration; acoustic observation depends on imported high-end ADCPs; optical current meters remain largely experimental. Advancing core sensor processes, long-term stability, innovation, and productization is essential for greater autonomy in ocean current measurement.

title: DOA Estimation Based on Fractional Fourier Transform Using Wideband Linear Chirps with Experimental Data
authors: Shuo Liu；Wen Zhang*；Yun Zhao；Zulong Chen
description: The paper validates FRFT-based DOA estimation for wideband LFM signals against FFT-based CBF, MVDR, and MUSIC using simulations and field data. FRFT concentrates chirp energy in the fractional domain and makes the array manifold approximately time-invariant. Simulations show FRFT-MVDR has higher resolution than FFT-MVDR, FRFT-MUSIC is more robust under low SNR and limited snapshots, while FRFT-CBF performs worse than FFT-CBF. Field experiments confirm FRFT-MVDR’s advantage, reducing average main-lobe width by 45.2% (from 12.3° to 6.73°) and significantly suppressing sidelobes.

title: Direction Tracking of Underwater Acoustic Target Based on FitNet Algorithm
authors: Zikun Meng；Wen Zhang*；Jian Shi；Qiankun Yu；Shuo Liu；Yan Liu
description: The paper proposes a FitNet-based direction-tracking method for underwater acoustic targets in complex marine environments. CBF is first applied to SWAP passive sonar data from a bottom-mounted 32-element array to extract target bearings and segment two trajectories. Kalman filtering and FitNet are then compared for direction tracking. FitNet achieves lower MSE for the nonlinear curved motion of Target 1, whereas Kalman filtering performs better on the linear segments of Target 2. The complementary results suggest potential for hybrid tracking systems that combine neural-network nonlinear learning with conventional signal processing.

title: Machine Learning-Based Approach for Single-Hydrophone Broadband Source Localization in Shallow Water Environment
authors: Yan Liu；Wen Zhang*；Jian Shi*；Qiankun Yu；Zikun Meng
description: The paper validates single-hydrophone broadband source localization in shallow water north of Elba using KRAKEN-generated replica fields and SACLANT93 data. A five-phase pipeline builds 651 simulated sources, extracts 150–200 Hz STFT features, and trains SVR and RF regressors for range–depth estimation. SVR consistently outperforms RF: for hydrophone 24, range MAPE is 0.66% versus 2.05%, and depth MAPE 0.41% versus 0.75%; array-wide, SVR achieves 1.31% range and 0.51% depth MAPE. Compared with MFP (5.43 km, 75.6 m), machine learning reduces localization error by about an order of magnitude, while RF may offer higher computational efficiency.

title: Research on low-noise amplification circuit for the front-end of nanovolt-level weak signal in eXpendable Current Profiler
authors: Yuanxi Zhao；Zibo Lu；Haoran Qin；Xinyu Wang；Wen Zhang*；Sheng Wu*
description: The paper proposes a low-noise multi-stage front-end amplification circuit for nanovolt-level XCP current signals. A differential transistor pair and parallel low-noise operational amplifiers form the core amplification chain, followed by a second-order bandpass filter centered at 16 Hz. LTspice simulations show that a 50 nV, 16 Hz input is amplified to about 80 mV, with gain exceeding 10⁶, signal-to-noise ratio better than 30 dB, and strong 16 Hz selectivity. The results are simulation-based but objective and repeatable, indicating the scheme meets practical XCP weak-current signal processing requirements.

title: Research on resonance-based high sensitivity seawater conductivity sensor
authors: Zibo Lu  ；Yuanxi Zhao；Haoran Qin ；Yuan Wang；Wen Zhang*；Sheng Wu*
description: The paper designs a high-sensitivity inductive seawater conductivity sensor using resonance compensation to address weak signals and difficult detection. Four dual-transformer compensation topologies—SS, SP, PS, and PP—are analyzed through equivalent-circuit and transfer-function models. SP compensation gives the highest output gain at resonance. Experiments with an inductive probe show best performance in 80–150 kHz; considering amplitude, anti-interference, and parameter matching, 97 kHz is selected. SP compensation improves output sensitivity by 8.34 times over the uncompensated model while suppressing environmental magnetic interference and circuit noise, supporting high-precision marine conductivity measurement.

title: Surface and Underwater Target Recognition in Mismatched Marine Environments Using Machine Learning
authors: Qiankun Yu；Wen Zhang*；Yan Liu；Shuo Liu；Zikun Meng
description: The paper examines surface and underwater target recognition under mismatched marine environments. A GBDT classifier is trained on KRAKEN-generated simulated data and tested on SACLANT 1993 measurements, using 30 m depth as the surface/underwater boundary. Numerical control experiments vary sediment density, thickness, and attenuation. Results show sediment density and thickness changes have negligible effects, while attenuation mismatch causes significant degradation. Counterintuitively, expanding the training set by varying environmental parameters reduces test accuracy, highlighting attenuation mismatch as a key robustness challenge for machine-learning recognition.

title: Fabrication and Electrical Characterization of XCP Electrode With Quasi-Nano Ag/AgCl Materials
authors: Guangyuan Chen , Qisheng Zhang , Haijing He , Libin Du, Lei Lin, and Wen Zhang
description: The paper fabricates an XCP electrode using quasi-nano Ag/AgCl material and builds a laboratory marine-current simulation system for moving-measurement tests. SEM shows AgCl particles below 500 nm, enlarging redox-active contact area to improve sensitivity and response. Static tests give an electrode drift of 6.7 nV/s, about 7.5 times better than the 50 nV/s XCP requirement, with 0.4 µV/s additional-field deviation. Dynamic tests at 5.14 cm/s show a 7% relative error between measured and calculated electric fields, validating the laboratory test method and its applicability to other current-simulation experiments.

title: Surface and underwater acoustic target recognition using only two hydrophones based on machine learning
authors: Qiankun Yu ; Wen Zhang ; Min Zhu; Jian Shi; Yan Liu; Shuo Liu
publication: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
description: The paper improves surface/underwater acoustic target recognition by combining GBDT with vertical-linear-array feature extraction using only two hydrophones. KRAKEN generates a large simulated training set from SACLANT 1993 environmental parameters, while VLA feature extraction assimilates heterogeneous simulated and experimental data and adds channel information beyond source spectra. The method addresses poor accuracy of some single hydrophones, achieving recognition accuracies of 1 and 0.9384 with two hydrophones, compared with only 0.4715 and 0.5620 for one hydrophone, and reports up to 100% accuracy on SACLANT 1993 data.

title: Impact of Typhoon Noise on the Detection Performance of Multi-Static Sonobuoy Array
authors: Yun Zhao*；Ruiting Qin；Shuo Liu；Wen Zhang
description: The paper evaluates how typhoon noise affects multi-static sonobuoy array detection. A performance model integrates the bi-static sonar equation with probability fusion, while the deep-sea noise field is simulated by coupling the Holland typhoon wind model, Wilson/Piggott wind-noise source-level models, and a typhoon-induced underwater noise field. Real typhoon and marine environmental data drive dynamic evaluation as the typhoon moves. Results show noise level near the multi-static system changes with typhoon motion and significantly degrades sonar detection performance, providing theoretical support for target stealth sailing under typhoon-noise concealment.

title: 海流探测仪器与技术研究现状及展望
authors: 康文慧1 , 徐东昕1 , 赵 强2 , 曲 轶1 , 张 文3 , 谢栋樑1
description: 梳理机械、电磁、声学多普勒、声学时差四类传统海流计，以及光纤光栅型、光纤干涉型新型海流计的探测原理、优缺点、应用领域与发展现状；指出海流探测正向高精度、智能化、集成化演进，并提出基于连续时差法的光致超声测流思路，为海流计研发与海洋探测技术升级提供参考。

title: Mesoscale eddy identification in the North Pacific based on DeepLabV3+
authors: Xiang GAO1 , Wen ZHANG1* , Ru CHEN2
description: The study applies DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation to identify mesoscale eddies in the North Pacific (140°E–180°E, 10°N–40°N) from Copernicus L4 sea surface height. Models are trained on 1993–2019 SSH, tested against 2023 AVISO eddy data, and used to map daily eddy distributions for January–June 2024. The resulting maps reveal eddy shape, propagation, generation, and dissipation: eddies are typically circular or elliptical under Coriolis effects; same-sign eddies merge, opposite-sign eddies repel and deform; propagation is modulated by background currents, depth, and topography; splitting and eddy–eddy interaction drive generation and decay. The work is image-based and case-focused, without quantifying energy, momentum, or vorticity balances.

title: Finite element simulation and experimental study of underwater low-frequency fluid sound source
authors: Fenghe Liu1 , Yun Zhao1*, Yuxin Xia2 , Zhicheng Wang1 , Simin Wang3 , Chunzheng Xi4 and Wen Zhang1
description: The paper develops an underwater low-frequency target-simulation device using a push-pull fluid sound source to mimic submarine acoustic radiation for sonar testing and deception. COMSOL finite-element fluid–acoustic coupling optimizes blade size, number, material, motor speed, swing amplitude, and exciting force, while giving power and pressure distributions. Simulations indicate five blades outperform three, aluminum alloy yields higher fundamental-frequency energy than stainless steel, the lowest frequency is 20.09 Hz, and 48° is the best swing amplitude. Experiments confirm stable low-frequency radiation, with received signals concentrated around 20–21 Hz from 0.5–5 m, supporting practical sonar-equipment testing.

title: Surface and Underwater Acoustic Source Recognition Using Multi-Channel Joint Detection Method Based on Machine Learning
authors: Qiankun Yu , Min Zhu *, Wen Zhang * , Jian Shi * and Yan Liu
publication: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
description: The paper proposes a machine-learning multi-channel joint detection method for surface/underwater acoustic source recognition. KRAKEN generates training data under SACLANT 1993 environmental settings for a 48-hydrophone VLA, while real sea-trial data are used for testing. kNN, RS-kNN, GBDT, and LightGBM are compared using module features and real/imaginary features. GBDT and LightGBM generally outperform kNN-based methods; module features often work better, though the best all-array result is GBDT with real/imaginary features, giving 42 hydrophones above 0.9 accuracy. Surface models reach pass rates of 40–41 for GBDT/LightGBM versus 30 for kNN-type models.

title: Striation-Based Broadband Source Localization Using a Particle Velocity Sensor in Deep Water
authors: Yanqun Wu , Wei Guo, Fuyin Wang , Bingbing Zhang , Wen Zhang , Shuidong Xiong, Qiong Yao, and Weihua Zhang
description: The paper localizes broadband deep-water sources with a single particle-velocity sensor using Lloyd’s-mirror striations. Under the reliable acoustic path, constructive/destructive interference tracks for pressure and PV fields are predicted from direct–surface-reflected delays, enabling pressure-array striation matching to extend to PV/AVS sensing. PV beamforming estimates azimuth and elevation; range follows from elevation, and about 3.2 dB array gain improves the intensity spectrogram. One-dimensional SPM matches frequency striations for near-instant depth estimates, while two-dimensional MSPM matches over range/time before frequency integration to raise SNR. Simulations and data show narrow main lobes, low-SNR robustness, and usefulness for shallow or distant sources with few striations.

title: Surface and Underwater Acoustic Source Recognition Using Array Feature Extraction Based on Machine Learning
authors: Qiankun Yu1 , Wen Zhang1*, Min Zhu1 , Jian Shi1 , Yan  Liu1 , Shuo Liu
description: The paper proposes an array-feature-extraction machine-learning method for surface/underwater acoustic source recognition. KRAKEN generates simulation data matched to SACLANT 1993, and covariance features between VLA channels are extracted from simulated and experimental data. A GBDT classifier is evaluated by accuracy, recall, F1, and accuracy across three frequency bands. The array-feature model alleviates poor accuracy of some single-channel classifiers and achieves good sea-trial performance, with experimental accuracies of 0.9920, 0.9857, and 0.9713 for the three bandwidths.

title: Simulation Study on Optimization Design of MEMS Hydrophone Based on AlN Film
authors: Qiankun Yu1 , Yongchao Zou1*, and Wen Zhang
description: The paper simulates and optimizes an AlN-film MEMS hydrophone using elastic-mechanics and sound–solid coupling models. Finite-element analysis compares circular and square diaphragms, showing the square shape improves overall sensitivity and frequency response. It then studies piezoelectric film radius and thickness, finding that increasing radius significantly improves sensitivity. Finally, sandwiched and unequal-thickness piezoelectric structures are compared, with unequal-thickness structures markedly improving device performance. The results provide design guidance for future high-performance AlN MEMS hydrophones.

title: Surface and Underwater Acoustic Source Discrimination Based on Machine Learning Using a Single Hydrophone
authors: Wen Zhang * , Yanqun Wu *, Jian Shi *, Hongze Leng, Yun Zhao and Jizhou Guo
publication: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
description: The paper implements supervised machine learning to discriminate surface and underwater acoustic sources using only one hydrophone in shallow water. KRAKEN generates simulated training data with SACLANT 1993 environmental settings. kNN, finely tuned random-subspace kNN, and ResNet-18 are evaluated using precision, recall, F1, and accuracy. ResNet-18 achieves the best precision–recall balance and reaches 1.0 accuracy on both simulated and experimental data. All 48 VLA hydrophones are then compared, showing random-subspace kNN performs best overall. The results demonstrate that machine learning can solve surface/underwater source discrimination effectively even with a single hydrophone.
